hints: Use the arc length formula $s = r\theta$ to find the angle $\angle AOB = \frac{\text{Arc } AB}{r}$.
Add $\angle AOB$ to the given angle $\angle AOC = \frac{\pi}{6}$ to find $\angle BOC$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the angle $\angle AOB$ in radians using the arc length formula $s = r\theta$ with $s = 2\text{ cm}$ and $r = 10\text{ cm}$:
$$\angle AOB = \frac{s}{r} = \frac{2}{10} = 0.2\text{ radians}$$

Add $\angle AOB$ to the angle $\angle AOC = \frac{\pi}{6}$ to determine the total angle $\angle BOC$:
$$\angle BOC = \angle AOC + \angle AOB = \frac{\pi}{6} + 0.2 = \frac{5\pi + 6}{30} \approx 0.724\text{ radians} \quad (\text{or } 41.5^\circ)$$

hints: In right-angled triangle $\triangle OBP$, find lengths $BP = 10\sin(\angle BOC)$ and $OP = 10\cos(\angle BOC)$.
Calculate the area of $\triangle OBP = \frac{1}{2} \times OP \times BP$.
Calculate the area of sector $BOC = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \angle BOC$.
Subtract the triangle area from the sector area to find the shaded area $BPC$.
walkthrough:
Find the perpendicular side lengths in the right-angled triangle $\triangle OBP$ with hypotenuse $OB = 10\text{ cm}$ and angle $\theta = \frac{5\pi+6}{30} \approx 0.7236\text{ rad}$:
$$BP = 10\sin\left(\frac{5\pi+6}{30}\right) \approx 6.6212\text{ cm}$$
$$OP = 10\cos\left(\frac{5\pi+6}{30}\right) \approx 7.4939\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the area of triangle $\triangle OBP$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle OBP) = \frac{1}{2} \times OP \times BP = \frac{1}{2} \times 7.4939 \times 6.6212 \approx 24.809\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of sector $BOC$ using $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } BOC) = \frac{1}{2} \times 10^2 \times \left(\frac{5\pi+6}{30}\right) = 50 \times 0.7236 \approx 36.180\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the triangle area from the sector area to obtain the shaded area $BPC$:
$$\text{Area}(BPC) = \text{Area}(\text{sector } BOC) - \text{Area}(\triangle OBP) = 36.180 - 24.809 = 11.371 \approx 11.4\text{ cm}^2$$
